title: Rogue-trajectory detector for usage/cost/latency with contextual explainers
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current alerting mostly flags single-metric spikes or threshold breaches; operators and SREs frequently need richer context to decide whether to page or silence an alert. We also see alerts that are short-lived or caused by distro shifts in small tenant cohorts that do not require escalation. Goal: build a backend service and pipeline stage that ingests usage/cost/latency telemetry and emits high-precision anomaly signals called 'rogue trajectories' plus compact contextual explainers that surface likely causes (tenant cohort, route, model variant, region, recent deploy) and an impact-probability score used for alerting/suppression.

Scope: implement a new detection service in the Console backend that runs immediately after existing aggregation and baselining steps in the analytics pipeline. The service will combine lightweight trajectory clustering, temporal smoothing, and a causal attribution pass (difference-in-distribution and short counterfactual perturbations) to produce a ranked list of candidate anomalies with rationale strings for display in Console and for downstream automated runbooks.
acceptance_criteria: Backend detector produces anomaly candidates for daily and intraday windows and writes to telemetry.anomalies topic with schema v1

Each anomaly includes: metric type (usage/cost/latency), primary dimension (tenant/route/model/region), start/end timestamps, confidence score (0-1), impact_probability (0-1), and a 1-2 sentence explainer string
Console UI can consume and display the explainer and the impact_probability; alerts for impact_probability >= 0.7 are eligible for paging by default
False positive rate on a 30-day held-out evaluation <= 8% for high-confidence anomalies (impact_probability >= 0.8) on historical labeled incidents
End-to-end latency from ingestion to anomaly output for intraday windows <= 90s for 95th percentile of events in standard cluster
Runbook action: when an anomaly is tagged as 'likely-deploy' and impact_probability >= 0.8, create a Jira ticket draft with prefilled context
design_decisions: Run detection as a stateless microservice that subscribes to intermediate aggregate topics rather than embedding logic into the stream processor to simplify rollout and A/B testing
Use lightweight k-shape inspired trajectory clustering for initial grouping, then apply a causal gradient attribution to rank potential drivers
Store full history of candidate anomalies in anomalies-store (S3 + metastore) for audits — only compact signals emitted to Kafka
Implement suppression heuristics that combine impact_probability, tenant-level exposure, and recent alert volume to avoid paging on noisy micro-anomalies
updates: 2026-02-12: Spike completed for k-shape clustering on a sampled week of usage metrics; basic clusters separate bursty tenants from gradual ramps (notes in Google Drive)
2026-02-18: Prototype explainer generator implemented (difference-of-distribution over route and model tags). Initial explainers produced terse natural language but need templating work

2026-02-24: Infra review - service will run in Console backend namespace with a dedicated consumer group. Scaling plan based on consumer lag thresholds agreed with infra team (PR: github.com/redwood/console/pull/4821)

2026-02-26: Ran offline evaluation against 90 days of labeled incidents. High-confidence recall is good for latency incidents but we still miss multi-tenant correlated billing regressions; plan to add cross-tenant correlation step
2026-03-01: Started integrating with alerts dispatcher; feature flag gating rollout. Need to finalize explainer templates and alert suppression defaults before can unflag
notes: We need to be careful about tenant PII in explainers — avoid echoing customer identifiers in free text. Use hashed cohort names or internal tenant-slugs only visible to authorized users.
Consider a 'dry-run' Console view for the first 2 weeks so SREs and a selected set of customers can opt into seeing signals without paging.
Retention: anomalies-store should keep raw signal payloads for 90 days and compact summaries for 1 year to support audits and model retraining
risks: Over-alerting causing pager fatigue if impact_probability calibration is off
Explainers that leak sensitive info if templates are too verbose
Performance regression in analytics pipeline if anomaly computation pulls large historical windows synchronously
Operational burden for noisy tenants — suppression tuning will require 2-3 iterations post-rollout
implementation_steps: 1) Add anomalies topic schema in Kafka (avro) and update schema registry
2) Implement detector service skeleton in console-backend repo with consumer/producer and feature flag
3) Implement clustering + attribution modules; wire to offline eval harness
4) Create explainer templating library and PII-safe renderers
5) Add suppression engine with configurable policies stored in config-service
6) End-to-end tests and performance benchmarks; create dashboard in Console for detector health
7) Rollout behind feature flag -> dry-run -> canary -> full based on signal quality
